pr_title: ARM64 intrinsic support for Vector64.Create() and Vector128.Create()
pr_body:
Added hardware intrinsic for various overloads of `Vector64.Create()` and `Vector128.Create()`:
* Multiple arguments - The APIs that takes multiple parameters to be set in respective lanes are implemented in C# using `AdvSimd.Insert`.
* Single arguments - The APIs that takes single argument and should be copied in all lanes are implemented in JIT by generating `dup`/`mov`/`fmov` instructions.

While I was there, I noticed an edge case where we hit assert if trying to emit an immediate `int.MaxValue`. Fixed it as well.

Contributes to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/33308 and https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/33496.
Fixes: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/35821
pr_comments:
@tannergooding  and @echesakovMSFT  - Just FYI, while working on something else I found 2 issues for which we don't have test coverage today.
1. `Vector64.Create((double)10)` (any integer value casted to `double`)
2. Passing `Vector64<double>` or `Vector64<long>` as parameter to a function.

I will fix and add test coverage for it before merging.

issue_context.title: Assertion failed '!"Didn't find a class handle for simdType"' when trying to pass Vector64<ulong> to function
issue_context.body:
If one of the `Vector64<ulong>`, `Vector<long>` or `Vector<double>` is on evaluation stack and is passed to a function, we hit assert [here](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/56518a7546bf2ad200936938e0f33cd07d54a378/src/coreclr/src/jit/hwintrinsic.cpp#L216).

```
Assertion failed '!"Didn't find a class handle for simdType"'
```

review_comments:
Shouldn't this tag (and the respective handling) be on `CreateScalar`?

The `Create(T value)` methods are for broadcasting, that is setting all elements of the vector to `value`.
Actually, I see that these are mapping to `dup` but then I'm not connecting how `fmov` and `movi` allow broadcasting the value
`CreateScalar()` intrinsify work is being done separately by @echesakovMSFT  in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/35300. This PR focuses on `Create()` methods.
Nevermind, I found the relevant instructions. There are a few variants of `fmov` and `movi` that I had missed.
yeah, these are specifically "C7.2.122 FMOV (vector, immediate)" and "C7.2.197 MOVI"
@kunalspathak You might want to add comment here in the same fashion as it's done for Sse2 case
Spoke offline and this is not needed.
I didn't know about #35037. I don't see any problem doing what you are suggesting given there are no much perf implication (and I don't think there will be any).

I think it might be better to make keep this intrinsic and have `DuplicateToVector128` share a codepath with it or forward to it as a helper.

The reasoning is that we will eventually want to support creating constants for all the various `Create` methods on both x86, x64, and ARM64 (and presumably ARM32 if that is ever supported).
The mapping of `Create` to underling intrinsics isn't necessarily 1-to-1 (especially on x86/x64 where containment and different paths exist depending on what ISAs are available).

So, as we add more paths to the JIT that use these intrinsics and even potentially look at introducing other optimizations that use the HWIntrinsics, it would be convenient to be able to just remember that `Vector128_Create` is what you use on either architecture for efficiently creating a vector.
